quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 (year ended December 31, 2025) results: revenue RMB1,033.6 million, up 91.6% from RMB539.5 million; gross profit RMB558.0 million (+110.5%), gross profit margin 54.0% vs 49.1%; loss for the year RMB1,003.7 million vs RMB892.4 million, including share-based payment expenses of RMB526.1 million; adjusted net loss (non-HKFRS) RMB437.7 million, narrowing 32.1%; R&D costs RMB974.2 million (+26.1%). Revenue came almost entirely from customers in the Chinese mainland (RMB1,033,362 thousand; Hong Kong RMB244 thousand). Cash and cash equivalents were RMB1,504.7 million at December 31, 2025 (RMB313.6 million a year earlier); the H shares were listed on the HKEX Main Board on January 8, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue RMB1,033.6 million (+91.6%); gross margin 54.0%; adjusted net loss RMB437.7 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY2025 revenue by product: GPGPU products RMB922.6 million (+149.6%, 89.3% of revenue) as GPGPU shipment volume rose 168.5%; training series (TG) RMB583.7 million (+116.7%) with training shipments up 131.5%, which the company attributes to customer demand especially for TG Gen 2, enhanced sales efforts and accelerated sales of TG Gen 1 inventories; inference series (ZK) RMB338.9 million (+238.2%) with inference shipments up 194.8% on rising market demand for inference products; AI computing solutions RMB96.1 million (-42.2%), attributed to the strategic prioritisation of the GPGPU business and the project-based, customized nature of solutions. Gross margins: GPGPU products 55.0% (56.6% in 2024); training series 64.2% (60.2%) on higher pricing driven by customer demand; inference series 39.2% (46.7%) on lower selling prices set to capture a larger market share and accelerate inventory sales; AI computing solutions 41.5% (31.7%).
quarterly_data.figure: GPGPU RMB922.6 million (+149.6%); TG RMB583.7 million (+116.7%); ZK RMB338.9 million (+238.2%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Customers (FY2025): the five largest customers accounted for approximately 43.0% of revenue and the largest customer approximately 16.1% (customers not named; Customer A RMB166,732 thousand in 2025, Customer B RMB242,181 thousand in 2024); 28% of trade and bills receivables and long-term trade receivables were due from the largest customer and 59% from the five largest. As of December 31, 2025 the group had served over 340 customers and its products and solutions had been deployed in over 1,000 projects across sectors including financial services, healthcare and transportation. Contract liabilities (advances received from customers for GPGPU products) rose to RMB126,908 thousand from RMB28,756 thousand.

quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain (FY2025 annual report): a fabless company, its suppliers are core manufacturing partners (foundries, OSAT partners and PCB assembly partners) and providers of memory components, IP cores, design software and technical services; the key items procured are wafers, memory components, substrates, EDA tools, chip tape-out services and PCB processing services. Purchases from the five largest suppliers were approximately 57.0% of total purchases and from the largest supplier approximately 32.9% (suppliers not named). The company says it runs a multi-vendor strategy with backup supplier arrangements for key categories and did not experience any material shortage, delays or quality issues in the supply of key components and manufacturing services during 2025. Capital commitments were RMB31.3 million at year-end (RMB56.4 million a year earlier).
quarterly_data.figure: Top five suppliers ~57.0% of purchases; largest ~32.9%

quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Software stack (FY2025): the company launched a new-generation software development platform natively compatible with mainstream GPU programming models, which it says improved code migration efficiency by more than 80%; its core acceleration library improved performance by generally more than 20% over the previous version; a large-model acceleration toolkit with lossless quantization improved long-text processing efficiency by more than 50%, raised system computing utilization by more than 60% and reduced cluster communication overhead by more than 30%, and the related technologies supported production-level cluster deployments for leading large-model developers (not named). The DeepSpark open-source community had adapted more than 610 mainstream algorithm models.
quarterly_data.figure: Code migration efficiency >80%; long-text processing efficiency >50%; >610 models adapted

quarterly_data.quarter: Iluvatar CoreX annual report: 2025 Annual Report (04-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management outlook (FY2025 annual report): the company sees leading internet enterprises and AI companies continuing to build large-scale training clusters with strong demand for training chips, while inference diversifies across cloud, edge and on-device, and says cluster interconnection has become a key competitive factor for clusters of tens of thousands of GPUs. Plans: develop the next-generation TG series (computational density, memory bandwidth and cluster scalability for large-scale training) and next-generation ZK series (edge-to-cloud inference, lower-precision and mixed-precision data types); deepen collaboration with CPU manufacturers, server OEMs, ISVs and cloud service providers; expand into intelligent driving, industrial manufacturing, intelligent terminals and smart agriculture; and extend the TY edge computing series in robotics and intelligent terminals. Chairperson's statement: the company will continue to increase investment in independent R&D and advance the development and mass production of next-generation computing products. The R&D team had more than 530 employees (759 full-time employees in total at December 31, 2025).
